sub.en: Look at the questions. Which quantifier goes with things you can count?

items.q: ___ rice do you need?
items.why: How much + uncountable. How many + countable plural.

items.q: ___ lemons are there?
There are ___ mushrooms in the fridge.
There isn’t ___ rice left.
items.why: much and many are used mostly in negatives and questions.

items.q: There aren’t ___ olives left.
Add ___ salt — just a small spoon.
items.why: a little + uncountable, a few + countable.

acts.title: Two countries, two plates
text: Papua New Guinea is a hundred and sixty kilometres north of Australia. It grows about three-quarters of its own food, and less than a quarter of its people live in cities. Most families have a small farm, so the ingredients for the evening meal are usually a few metres from the kitchen.

Singapore is the opposite. It grows less than ten per cent of its food and imports almost everything else. There isn’t much space for farms — the whole country is smaller than many cities. But you can eat food from twenty countries in one street, and a meal costs a few dollars.

Neither country is unusual. Half the world grows most of its own food; the other half buys it. The interesting question is not how much a country grows, but how many people know where their dinner came from.

write.q: Write a simple recipe: 6 steps. Use at least four cooking verbs and four quantifiers (a lot of, a little, a few, too much, not enough, how much/many).
write.model: First, boil three hundred grams of rice in a saucepan with a little salt. Chop a few mushrooms and two onions. Fry them in a hot pan for five minutes — don’t use too much oil. Add the rice and mix everything together. If there isn’t enough water, add a little more. Serve it hot with a lot of fresh herbs.

speak.q: Explain a dish you cook out loud in five steps. Then answer: How much does it cost? How many people does it feed?
speak.model: First, I chop a few onions and fry them. Then I add the rice and a little salt. I boil it for twenty minutes. I don’t add too much water. Finally I serve it with beef. It costs about two thousand tenge and it feeds four people.
